findings.title: The Web-ii gate was recorded before the master merge and was not re-run at the subject head
findings.claim: Every gate result is for head b532961f, which predates the merge. The ledger still says SIM_VERSION 53, but HEAD 67d6534d merges master at SIM 54 (own-ship-window and asteroids-ii). Nothing records typecheck, npm test, determinism, test:web-output, test:web-net or the Electron runtime gates at the head that is about to merge.
findings.evidence: plan L2742 ('SIM_VERSION 53, no diff vs merge-base'), plan L2754 ('Head b532961f'), docs/gates.md:L945 ('Web-ii gate (Task 12), head b532961f'). git log order: a0652198 'docs(web-ii): gate results' comes before 67d6534d 'merge: master into web-ii (… SIM 54)'.
findings.why: Check 14 asks whether the merged master code still passes through the web paths. The merge brought renderer changes under main.ts, the console maps and the asteroid sim into a branch whose browser, Electron and determinism gates have only run without them. The recorded SIM number is also now wrong.
findings.fix: At 67d6534d (or the final head), re-run npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run test:determinism, npm run test:web-output, npm run test:web-net plus the origin-refused injection, and the seven Electron runtime gates. Update the plan's ledger (L2733-L2754) and docs/gates.md:L945 with the new head and SIM 54.

findings.title: Uncaught errors from the Electron guest are found only by parsing a debug-only log line, with no check that the parser ever matched
findings.claim: createElectronPlayer counts the Electron guest's uncaught page errors only by regex-matching the FTL_DEBUG 'DBG console <level> <msg>' stderr lines. Nothing asserts that any DBG line was seen. If that debug-only format changes (level printed differently, prefix renamed, the event signature moves), `errors` stays empty and scenario.ts:L138-L139 passes silently. The driver's own comment still says FTL_DEBUG is 'never set by the gates', which invites exactly that kind of change.
findings.evidence: scripts/web/net/players.ts:L157 (FTL_DEBUG: '1'), L170-L177 (regex /^DBG console (?:error|3) (.*)$/, only 'Uncaught' lines become errors); scripts/network/online-app-smoke.cjs:L5 ('Local debugging only (FTL_DEBUG=1, never set by the gates)'), L84 (console.error('DBG console', d.level, …)); scripts/web/net/scenario.ts:L138-L139 (the only page-error assertion).
findings.why: The chromium-electron pairing is the only gate with a real Electron page in mixed play. A silent undercount there means an Electron page exception during rehost or reconnect would pass the browser gate. This is the risk check 13 names.
findings.fix: Rewrite online-app-smoke.cjs:L5 to say the web-net gate sets FTL_DEBUG and parses the 'DBG console' and 'DBG loaded' lines as a contract. In createElectronPlayer, record that at least one 'DBG loaded ' line was parsed, and have launch() or runPairing fail with 'electron console not watched' when none was. Optionally emit a fixed non-debug marker, such as APP_PAGE_UNCAUGHT from the console-message handler at L85, and match that instead of the debug format.

findings.title: The transport regression test covers only closeAttempt, not the peer-loss path the fix was for
findings.claim: The new unit test asserts the close PortFrame only after closeAttempt('live'). The product bug was a guest leaving, which reaches retire() through the 'failed'/'closed' wire response (owner.ts:L50) and through the replace path (L85). Neither path has a unit assertion on the frame, and nothing checks that a second retire of the same entry sends no second frame.
findings.evidence: tests/rtcTransportOwner.test.ts:L102-L113 (closeAttempt only); src/network/transport/owner.ts:L26 (early return on re-retire), L30 (the new postMessage), L50 (response path), L85 (rtc-replaced).
findings.why: The web-net gate does cover peer loss end to end (scenario.ts:L89, host pauses for the lost guest), so this is not blocking. But the unit test that claims to guard b532961f does not run the branch that regressed.
findings.fix: Add cases to rtcTransportOwner.test.ts. Reply 'closed' (and 'failed') to a ready attempt's request and expect exactly [{ version: 1, type: 'close', reason: 'rtc-attempt-failed' }] on port2. Start a second attempt for the same remote and expect one 'rtc-replaced' frame on the old port. After closeAttempt plus its 'closed' reply, expect frames.length to stay 1.

findings.title: The output check of the bundled middleware asks only about static file paths
findings.claim: checkWebOutput asks the bundled index.js about each walked static path, as GET. It never asks about '/', an unknown path, a path with a query string, or a HEAD request. Only the source-level unit test covers '/', and it is GET only.
findings.evidence: scripts/web/web-output.ts:L49 (paths come only from walk(staticDir)), L63-L67; tests/webPasscode.test.ts:L15 (PATHS includes '/' but no query or unknown path), L11 (GET only).
findings.why: The deployed artifact is the esbuild bundle, not passcode.ts. The code reading is correct (handlePasscode uses only pathname, passcode.ts:L76, and the cookie check at L87). Still, the check meant to prove 'every request needs the cookie' should exercise the request shapes Vercel actually forwards.
findings.fix: In checkWebOutput, also ask '/', '/no-such-file', '/index.html?x=1' and a HEAD of '/assets/authorityWorker.js', each without the cookie (expect a 401 with the form) and with it (expect isNext).

findings.title: Nothing in the repo makes a non-prebuilt `vercel` deploy fail
findings.claim: D2 relies on the owner always using deploy:web (`vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod`). If someone runs plain `vercel --prod` or `vercel deploy --prod` in the linked checkout, the CLI uploads the source tree and Vercel builds it with its default preset. That deploy would have no Routing Middleware, so whatever it serves has no passcode in front. No .vercelignore or vercel.json in the branch makes such a deploy fail.
findings.evidence: package.json:L12 (the only scripted path is --prebuilt); docs/gates.md:L927-L934 (owner steps say to use deploy:web); the diff file list (.superpowers/sdd/web-ii-impl.diff L79-L3022) adds no .vercelignore or vercel.json.
findings.why: This is operator error outside the scripted path, so it is not P0. But the cost is the private site served without its passcode, and the guard is cheap.
findings.fix: Add a root .vercelignore containing '/*' (a --prebuilt deploy uploads only .vercel/output, so it is unaffected), or a vercel.json whose buildCommand exits non-zero with 'use npm run deploy:web'. Add a line to docs/gates.md step 4.

verified: Passcode compare is constant time: both sides are hashed with SHA-256 and XOR-folded over 32 bytes (src/web/passcode.ts:L52-L56). The cookie MAC uses crypto.subtle.verify (L42). The regex limits the cookie to 1-12 digits and a 43-char base64url MAC, and the MAC must decode to 32 bytes (L36-L41).

Expiry window enforced both ways: expiry > now && expiry <= now + 30 days (passcode.ts:L39). Tests cover expired, expires-exactly-now and a valid MAC whose expiry is beyond 30 days (tests/webPasscode.test.ts:L42-L58).

Fail closed: a missing or empty passcode, or a secret that is missing, not base64 or under 32 bytes, gives a 503 on every request (passcode.ts:L23-L26, L74-L75; test L59-L64). A wrong code sleeps 1 s and returns 401 'Wrong passcode' (L84-L85). A right code gives a 303 to '/' with the exact cookie attributes from spec L243 (L79-L83; test L37).

No path bypasses the passcode: handlePasscode only passes a request with a valid cookie on a path other than /__pass (passcode.ts:L87). Every other request, at any path, including '/', unknown paths and paths with query strings (only pathname is read, L76), gets the 401 form page.

config.json runs the middleware first on '/(.*)' with continue, then 'private, no-cache' for all paths, then 'no-store' for /version\.json (scripts/web/web-output.ts:L14-L18). .vc-config.json has runtime edge and envVarsInUse [FTLITE_PASSCODE, FTLITE_COOKIE_SECRET] (L20). checkWebOutput deep-compares both, refuses a static __pass and networkTransport.html, and imports and calls the bundled functions/_middleware.func/index.js with a throwaway env (L41-L72). tests/webOutput.test.ts proves that a pass-through middleware and a reordered route both fail the check.
Middleware is bundled with esbuild (platform neutral, ESM), so process.env stays as written for the Edge runtime (web-output.ts:L23-L29; src/web/middleware.ts:L5-L8), per W-8.

--test and --allow-missing-paid cannot reach .vercel/output. Every test-only flag throws without --test (build/webBuild.ts:L14, L24). A --test outDir must be strictly under out/ or tmpdir with a trailing separator, so out/, tmpdir itself and '.vercel/output' are refused (L38-L40; tests/webBuildPlan.test.ts:L33-L39). Production always gets packaged:true and no test fields (L36). deploy:web always runs a fresh production build:web, then check-output, then --prebuilt --prod (package.json:L12). buildWeb rmSyncs only plan.outDir (scripts/web/build-web.ts:L14).

IndexedDB: the only open call in src is openFtliteDatabase at version 2 (src/network/online/recordStore.ts:L18; grep found no other indexedDB.open). onupgradeneeded only creates missing stores, so a v1 'records' store survives (L19). onblocked rejects, and a late success is closed at once (L20-L22). Both stores set onversionchange to close and drop their cached connection (recordStore.ts:L41; duelRecordStore.ts:L22). Tests cover the v1-to-v2 upgrade keeping seat-v1 and mirror-v1 byte for byte, blocking by a v1 connection that will not close, and closing on a v3 request (tests/recordStore.test.ts diff L2183-L2223). In Electron, duelRecords stays unused (main.ts:L109-L110).

Start-up cannot hang or throw. acquireOnlineLock is raced against a 2 s timeout, never throws (sync throw and rejection both map to 'unavailable'), and releases a late grant (src/renderer/src/app/web/onlineLock.ts:L20-L48). A busy lock is retried once with a 1.5 s signal (L38). checkBrowserSupport is a pure typeof check (browserSupport.ts:L14-L22). Single player stays available when unsupported (Home.tsx:L12; tests/webStartupUi.test.tsx). The lock is released in the non-persisted pagehide teardown (main.ts:L216).

Teardown runs once, guarded by tornDown, and returns early on event.persisted (main.ts:L209-L217). pageSession registers its own non-persisted pagehide release before main.ts's listener, so releaseForUnload runs first (pageSession.ts:L105-L106). The leave prompt is installed only when window.ftlite is absent (main.ts:L198), and Electron main also allows will-prevent-unload (src/main/index.ts:L49). The pagehide teardown is the same list beforeunload used to run, plus the new web items (diff L1684-L1696). appExit.ts is untouched by the diff.

Fullscreen: if fullscreen exits while keyboard.lock() is pending, the fullscreenchange handler calls keyboard.unlock() (browserFullscreen.ts:L33). Per the Keyboard Lock API this rejects the pending lock, so locked becomes false (L46). The fallback Escape needs !wasLocked, no page exit within 1000 ms (set around exitFullscreen, L48-L49, reset on rejection) and no Escape keydown within 100 ms (L28, L34). All are tested (tests/webFullscreen.test.ts diff L2459-L2483).

The transport fix posts { version:1, type:'close', reason } on entry.port before closePort, inside retire's identity guard, so a re-retire sends nothing (src/network/transport/owner.ts:L25-L31). A controller portLink close after it goes to a closed port, and one before it makes the later post a no-op, so there is no duplicate frame. The regression test asserts the exact frame on the far port (tests/rtcTransportOwner.test.ts:L111). owner.ts is outside the content-digest manifest (build/contentDigest.ts:L12-L16).

Browser gates: commonPublication matches runId, sequence, tick and hash (scripts/web/net/scenario.ts:L25-L28). The stored mirror-v1 is read straight from IndexedDB after reopen and before Multiplayer and Reconnect (L111-L120). The origin-refused injection must show the chromium-host lobby failure, 403 evidence for the page's Origin (from Playwright/CDP, or a failed POST plus a 403 on Node's probe) and no successful create, else it exits 2 (web-net-smoke.ts:L85-L97). Reload keeps the Web Lock (scenario.ts:L92), and the leave prompt is asserted when the host closes (L105-L106).

Version banner: version.json is fetched with no-store and same-origin credentials at start and every 300 s, only on the menu or in a lobby, never in Single player (versionWatch.ts:L23-L42). It compares build.version, build.rev, build.sim, sim and digest (W-9, L19-L21). The banner reads 'New version: reload' and is hidden while playing (Menu.tsx:L36).

Spec texts are exact: UNSUPPORTED_TEXT, SAFARI_NOTE and ONE_TAB_TEXT (browserSupport.ts:L3-L5), 'Wrong passcode' (passcode.ts:L5), 'Download playtest log' (Settings.tsx:L39), and the file name ftlite-playtest-<first>-to-<last>.jsonl, oldest first (duelRecordStore.ts:L46-L51).

No new master code bypasses createPageOnline or the page guards. window.ftlite is read only in main.ts, leavePrompt.ts and browserFullscreen.ts (grep over src/renderer/src). There is a single IndexedDB opener. main.ts still builds pageOnline only through createPageOnline (main.ts:L102-L103).

Whether a page holding the ftlite-online Web Lock can enter Firefox's back-forward cache with the lock still held. If it can, a second tab would see 'busy' until eviction. Chrome blocks bfcache for pages with Web Locks; this was not checked for Firefox.
